approach: In `planning_round` (crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs:138-155) choose the planner's model and effort per call. Round 1 with 0 mechanical passes keeps today's values: `ctx.reading.producer_model` and `effort_for(Planner)`. When `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`, call a new `Models::planner_revision_setting(model, ordinary_effort)` in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs. It takes the model from `producer_setting(model, true).0`. It takes the effort from `hard_producer_effort` only when that is set, and otherwise keeps the ordinary effort passed in, so a config with no `hard_producer_*` is unchanged. After `agent_spec` builds the spec, set `spec.effort`, the same override pattern as producer.rs:338-341. The planner status line also prints the effort, and the invocation record already stores `spec.model` and `spec.effort`, so a run's output and records show the escalation. The critic, reader and verifier are untouched. Tests: one config unit test, three core tests that record the planner's model and effort per call, and one cli test. Then add a CHANGELOG entry, a spec.toml sentence and an appended decision D179.

decisions.choice: Add `Models::planner_revision_setting(model, ordinary_effort)` in config.rs, built on `producer_setting(.., true)` for the model. For the effort it uses `hard_producer_effort` only when that is set, and otherwise returns the ordinary effort passed in.
decisions.reason: The planner's ordinary effort is `verifier_effort` (config.rs:830-836), not `producer_effort`. `producer_setting(.., true)` falls back to `producer_effort` when no hard effort is set (config.rs:354-356). Calling it directly would silently change the planner's effort in a config with no hard setting, which breaks 'unchanged when unset' and criterion 3. The rule sits in the data crate next to `producer_setting`, and config.rs is a listed deliverable.

rejected.option: Call `producer_setting(model, true)` inline in planning.rs and use both results
rejected.why: It falls back to `producer_effort` when no hard effort is set. That can differ from the planner's `verifier_effort`, so a config with no hard setting would change the planner's effort.

rejected.option: Add a new config key such as `[job_plan] revision_model`
rejected.why: The brief rules out new config keys. The existing hard producer setting is what the request means by a stronger model.

decisions.choice: Escalate when `round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0`. A seed revision in round 1, pass 0 stays at the ordinary setting.
decisions.reason: This is the brief's definition of a critic revise or mechanical send-back, and `Attempt` already carries both counters. A seed revision is the first attempt within this job.

rejected.option: Also escalate when a `seed` revision is present
rejected.why: The criteria say round 1, pass 0 keeps the current setting. A retry's first call is not planning thrash within this job.

rejected.option: Escalate only after a critic revise
rejected.why: The request and the reading name both the critic revise and the mechanical plan-rule revision.

decisions.choice: Print the effort in the planner status line: `planner    {model} · {effort} · {wall}s · {cost}`. Leave the critic line unchanged.
decisions.reason: With the repository config the hard model equals the default model and the hard effort equals the planner's ordinary effort, so an effort-only escalation shows only in the effort on the line or in the record. A search for `planner    ` in *.rs and *.md found only planning.rs:175.

rejected.option: Leave the line as is and rely on the invocation record
rejected.why: The criterion allows either, but the owner reads the run's output first. A model-only line cannot show an effort-only escalation.

decisions.choice: Demonstrate criterion 5 with the workspace test run as the command, together with `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` run as separate simple commands on the final tree.
decisions.reason: The brief wants each check as its own simple command. The workspace test run is the one that exercises the new behavior tests and the doc-format rules (decision log, spec.toml, budgets), so it is the one with a seam and a fails-without.

rejected.why: The recorded checks use different flags (`--locked`, `-D warnings`) and the verifier can run the plain commands directly.

steps: Read config.rs:343-359 and add `Models::planner_revision_setting(&self, model: &str, ordinary_effort: &str) -> (String, String)`. It returns `(self.producer_setting(model, true).0, self.hard_producer_effort.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| ordinary_effort.to_string()))`. Doc-comment it: it escalates only what is configured, and it is unchanged when neither `hard_producer_*` is set.

Add a unit test in the config.rs test module, next to `producer_setting_escalates_only_a_hard_job` (config.rs:1082): `planner_revision_setting_takes_the_hard_model_and_effort_only_when_set`. Cover both set, only the model set, only the effort set, and neither set. In the neither case, the result must equal the inputs even when `producer_effort` differs from the ordinary effort passed in.

In planning.rs `planning_round`, replace `let model = ctx.reading.producer_model.clone();` (line 138) with a block. Compute `let ordinary_effort = jc.config.effort_for(Role::Planner).to_string();` and `let revised = round > 1 || mechanical_passes > 0;`. Take `(model, effort) = if revised { jc.config.models.planner_revision_setting(&ctx.reading.producer_model, &ordinary_effort) } else { (ctx.reading.producer_model.clone(), ordinary_effort) }`. Add a comment saying a revision is a thrashing plan, and that a seed revision in round 1, pass 0 is the first attempt of the job.

After `self.agent_spec(...)` (planning.rs:140-155) make the spec `let mut spec` and set `spec.effort = effort.clone();`. Change the status line (planning.rs:174-178) to `planner    {model} · {effort} · {:.0}s · {}`. Leave `critic_round` untouched.

In tests.rs, add `fn repo_with_planning_and_models(max_rounds, hard_effort: Option<&str>, hard_model: bool)`, refactoring `repo_with_config` (tests.rs:299) so the config text can be edited first. Add a recording wrapper `fn recording(settings: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(Role, String, String)>>>, script: Script) -> Script` that pushes `(spec.role, spec.model.clone(), spec.effort.clone())` and then calls the inner script. Put no escalation logic in the wrapper.

Add the tests of criteria 2 and 3 in tests.rs, next to the planning tests (tests.rs:1306-1528). Test 1, `a_planner_called_again_after_a_critic_revise_runs_at_the_hard_setting`: planner queue `[good_plan(), good_plan()]`, critic `[revising_critique(), accepting_critique()]`, `hard_producer_effort` set to `max`. Assert planner call 1 is `("claude-haiku-5-5", verifier_effort)` and call 2 is `(hard_producer_model, "max")`, read from the parsed `Config`, and assert the same from `Records::load` invocations filtered by `Role::Planner`. Test 2, `a_mechanical_revision_escalates_the_next_planner_call`: planner `[bad_plan(), good_plan()]`, critic `[accepting_critique()]`. Test 3, `without_a_hard_producer_setting_every_planner_call_keeps_the_same_model_and_effort`: no `hard_producer_*` lines, planner `[bad_plan(), good_plan(), good_plan()]`, critic `[revising_critique(), accepting_critique()]`. Assert all planner calls record the same model and effort, and that the effort is `verifier_effort`.

Add the drain.rs test `the_planner_after_a_revise_shows_the_hard_setting_in_its_line_and_its_record` near `a_hard_reading_gets_the_stronger_producer_setting...` (drain.rs:7930). Build the config from `common::test_config()` with `hard_producer_effort = "high"` replaced by `"max"`, plus `
[job_plan]
enabled = true
`. Set `scenario.critiques` to an inline revise and an inline accept and leave `plans` empty so the deterministic planner answers. Run with `Fixture::with_config`, `ask` and `go` using a `Lines` Ui. Assert the two `planner    ` lines and the two planner invocation records from `Records::load`.

Add the CHANGELOG.md entry (Unreleased / Added) in plain words. When the critic sends a plan back, or Athena's own plan rules send it back, the next planner call runs at the configured hard producer model and effort. First attempts, the critic, reader and verifier are unchanged. With no `hard_producer_*` setting nothing changes. The planner line now names the effort. Name the tests.
Add one sentence to the OLY-B-STD-02 `mechanism` string in docs/spec.toml (line 2349), saying a revised plan runs the planner at the `[models] hard_producer_*` setting. Keep it a single TOML line.

Append `## D179 · A revised plan runs the planner at the hard producer setting` at the end of docs/decisions.md, after D178's Provenance bullet, in the D177 shape: Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance. The Provenance bullet says Read: planning.rs, config.rs `producer_setting`, producer.rs:339-341, reading.rs:869-871; Measured: the new tests; Not measured: a real model run and the effect on planning rounds. Do not touch the existing bytes.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo test -p athena-data`, `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-cli`, then as separate commands `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace`.

risks.risk: The effort has no visible effect in the repository's own config, because the hard effort equals the planner's ordinary effort. The owner may see no change in a real run and think the change failed.
risks.mitigation: The tests use distinct values by editing the config text. The status line and the invocation record show the effort. The CHANGELOG entry and D179 say the effect depends on the configured hard setting.

risks.risk: A stronger model on revised calls costs more, and the planner cap `planner_usd` is unchanged.
risks.mitigation: The caps, timeouts and budget preflight (planning.rs:113) apply per call as before. The change adds no extra call and does not change `max_rounds` or `MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES`.

risks.risk: The test repository helper that rewrites athena.toml text could produce a config that fails validation, such as an unknown effort level.
risks.mitigation: The helper only replaces `hard_producer_effort = "high"` with a valid level (`max`, in `EFFORT_LEVELS`, config.rs:337) and removes the two `hard_producer_*` lines for the unset case. A missing hard model is allowed (`Option`, config.rs:328). A wrong replacement fails at config load on the first run.

risks.risk: A test asserting the exact `planner    ` line elsewhere would break when the effort is added to it.
risks.mitigation: A search of *.rs and *.md for the planner line prefix found no other assertion. `cargo test --workspace` in criterion 5 would show any miss.

demonstrations.observes: Planner call 1 records the reading's producer model (`claude-haiku-5-5` from `base_script`, tests.rs:232) and the planner's ordinary effort (`verifier_effort`). Planner call 2, after the revise, records `hard_producer_model` and `hard_producer_effort`. The test config replaces `hard_producer_effort = "high"` with `"max"` so the values differ. The invocation records hold the same model and effort.
